facts.text: The Pueblo of Tesuque dates back to at least 1200 AD, making it one of the oldest continuously inhabited sites in the region.
The name Tesuque comes from a Tewa word meaning 'village of the narrow place of the cottonwood trees,' reflecting the area's natural features.
The Pueblo was abandoned after the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, but the current community reestablished itself in the 18th century.
Tesuque is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, recognizing its cultural and historical significance.
The town has inspired writers and artists, appearing in novels such as Aldous Huxley's 'Brave New World' and being the setting for Michael Tobias's 'The Adventures of Marigold'.
Photography is prohibited inside the Pueblo, preserving its sacred spaces and historic architecture.
